findings.original: For position analysis, an ideal causal ReLU replaces one selected converted activation while leaving the graph, weights, and incoming converted computation fixed. It is a continuous diagnostic. Restoring all six sites reproduces the ANN; an empty intervention reproduces the conversion. Group effects are nonadditive because interventions alter subsequent computation.
findings.suggested_action: VERIFY against comparison/interval/design; no automatic deletion

findings.original: At one tick, fixed-GCN conversion falls to $71.44\pm2.80\%$ on MNIST and $46.80\pm1.22\%$ on CIFAR10. Which sites cause this gap? Figure~\ref{fig:positions} shows conditional recovery on the full 5,000-graph validation split for each teacher. The first node site closes 54.08\% and 23.54\% of the disagreement gap, measured per teacher and then averaged. Recovering all four node sites closes 80.4\% and 45.2\%; the two readout sites close 8.8\% and 14.9\%. The first site is the largest single-site accuracy recovery on both tasks. This locates a useful intervention point, but the recovery uses a continuous response and imposes no finite-event constraint.
findings.suggested_action: VERIFY against comparison/interval/design; no automatic deletion

findings.original: The distinction also matters for event allocation. Actual-message allocation costs 0.834/0.991 ms per graph versus local allocation's 0.668/0.806 in its own matched timing experiment. Exact local codeword exchanges can change downstream events even when first-site counts are fixed. Thus neither low $T$, local sparsity, nor the projected additions in Fig.~\ref{fig:centered} is a complete efficiency claim. A useful conversion must specify its event type, continuous work, prefix requirements, and backend.
